figures.caption: Figure 3: Importing .vtk simulation files into ParaView Initially, the particles will be populated as white point particles. The particles can be changed to be displayed according to their force, velocity, point ID, tangential velocity, radius, or mass. Point Gaussian is the preferred method to view the particles at their actual sizes. Select the particles in the pipeline

figures.caption: Figure 5: Velocity distributions Alternatively, the raw data file can be saved as a .csv file, which can be imported into Excel or Matlab for analysis or further post processing. This is performed by File>Save Data. In order to evaluate the mass flow rate of particles, an extra set of commands are placed in the input script. This command requires that a planar object be created using a CAD program. It works by counting how many particles pass through the face, their sizes, and their masses.
